cells.tense: Right now, with the pen, this is settling into something you can hold steadily.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Pick the piece of your setup that is finished enough, tell yourself it is done — then turn to the part that is not finished and give it the next hour.
cells.core: In how a piece of work is set up, you are letting something settle and it is holding — the leaning into tending is steady, so no running commentary is needed to keep it together. That steadiness is the sign the tightness has relaxed into ordinary attention, and what you are learning meets the structure instead of fighting it. What this balance can feed next is release that follows naturally once a stretch is complete, so it does not all have to be carried at once. Pick the piece that is finished — a step, a corner of the setup, one day's work — and call it through. That frees the next thing to begin without a ceremony, and the work you do after it is lighter for it.
cells.sheetLine: You can let a finished thing be finished and turn.
cells.verb: learning by tending a piece of the world
cells.place: your say over how a working thing is set up

cells.tense: Soon the whole arrangement will need to be right before anything is opened.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Before you decide the next shape of a piece of your setup, pause and sense what could happen, then say one sentence to yourself about it and leave the sentence unfinished.
cells.core: The shape of the work is getting built before the pieces are in hand, and the building keeps getting heavier. You are staging a next version of things that have not happened yet, and the detail is load-bearing; more of it goes on each time you sit down to it. From the inside, each addition is prudent. From the outside, the whole arrangement reads as a brace against being shown anything. Careful tending is not the same as refusing to let the thing breathe, and whoever stands near the setup can feel the difference between a plan and a grip. What this balance is for is growth happening without forcing, holding space without clutching. Set one corner of it down. Sense the next step without writing it out.

cells.tense: You were the one studying how it was built, and that was a while back.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Ask someone a beginner's question about something you once knew well — what is this actually for, or how does this part work — and listen without correcting their answer.
cells.core: The curiosity is still in you, but it is standing behind the last place it was used. You know the shape a thing should take here, and knowing it has become the reason not to touch the material. Somewhere you stopped sitting with the material as a student and started standing over it as someone who already knows how it should go. That gap is where the appetite for beginning used to live. It did not leave; you did not arrive with it. What this line carries is care that does not exhaust, holding space without clutching. Start something small tonight with no destination. Let the hands do a piece of work before the overview asks to be right.

cells.tense: You are already holding the structure steady, and the holding is not being counted.
cells.act: bear the duty and know when to let go
cells.ask: Name one part of the setup you have been holding that can stand without you for a week — then stop tending it and see what happens.
cells.core: The structure under this work is steady, and the steadying is not something you would call yours. You hold the arrangement, the thing that keeps the work possible, and in your account the structure just happens to be there. Look at what has been kept standing by your attention: the calendared hour, the way the pieces are stored, the habit that keeps the thing itself findable. None of it runs without someone holding it, and the someone has been you. What this balance is for is growth without forcing, care that does not tire, a grip that does not clutch. Decide what part of the work is finished and stop carrying it this week. Ask someone else to keep the hour.
